lines.text: A small island scented with nutmeg, fought over by empires, shaken by revolution and invasion. This is the story of Grenada, the spice island.
In 1650, French settlers came ashore, and a town grew round a horseshoe harbour that became the capital, St George's.
Britain took the island in 1763. In 1795, Julien Fedon led a rebellion against British rule that held much of the island for over a year.
Eric Gairy, born in 1922, would lead the island to independence as its first prime minister.
Maurice Bishop, born in 1944, would overthrow Gairy in the revolution of 1979, only to be killed by his own rivals.
In 1974, Grenada became independent from Britain, a nation known around the world for its nutmeg.
Dickon Mitchell, born in 1978, would become prime minister in 2022.
In October 1983, days after Bishop was murdered, American troops invaded the island.
Kirani James, born in 1992, would win Grenada's first Olympic gold, in the four hundred metres in London.
In 2004, Hurricane Ivan struck, damaging nine homes in every ten.
And in 2024, Hurricane Beryl wrecked the sister islands of Carriacou and nearby Union Island.
Through revolution, invasion and storms, the spice island keeps rebuilding.
